story: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District moves an AI academic honesty regulation and a separate screen time technology policy through committee in the two weeks before its 2026-27 school year opens, after already buying a classroom AI tool

claims.claim: The KPBSD Policy Review Committee meeting of August 3, 2026 was scheduled to start at 10:00 AM.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The August 3rd Policy Review Committee meeting was held in the Betty J. Glick Assembly Chambers in Soldotna.
claims.verbatim: Betty J. Glick Assembly Chambers, 144 N. Binkley Street, Soldotna, Alaska 99669
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The August 3rd Policy Review Committee agenda carried eight numbered policy or exhibit documents across four review sections.
claims.verbatim: AR 6161.5 High-Quality Instruction and Purposeful Use of Technology
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District
claims.notes: The eight are Exhibit 5123, AR 5131.9, BP 6000, BP 6141, BP 6161.1, AR 6161.1, BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5.

claims.claim: AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty appeared on the August 3rd committee agenda under the heading Policy Review-Ongoing.
claims.verbatim: 3. Policy Review-Ongoing
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The district describes AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty as a new administrative regulation brought forward in relation to the inclusion of AI.
claims.verbatim: AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty is a new Administrative Regulation presented to committee on 07-06-2026 at the recommendation from Administration, in relation to the inclusion of AI.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: Two competing drafts of AR 5131.9 were posted to the August 3rd agenda item, one from Administration and one from board member VanBuskirk.
claims.verbatim: VERSION 2 VANBUSKIRK AR 5131.9 Academic Honesty.pdf
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The Policy Review Committee postponed AR 5131.9 at its July 6, 2026 meeting and carried it to the next committee meeting.
claims.verbatim: Committee postponed this Administrative Regulation to the next Policy Review Committee meeting.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The Administration draft of AR 5131.9 opens by tying academic honesty directly to artificial intelligence.
claims.verbatim: The Kenai Peninsula Borough School District acknowledges the significance of academic honesty and the evolving role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in educational settings.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft

claims.claim: The AR 5131.9 draft makes misuse of AI tools a violation of academic honesty subject to discipline under BP 5144.
claims.verbatim: Inappropriate and/or misuse of AI tools will be considered a violation of academic honesty and subject to disciplinary action in accordance with BP 5144.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft

claims.claim: The AR 5131.9 draft reserves the district's right to monitor and review student use of AI tools.
claims.verbatim: The District reserves the right to monitor and review the use of AI tools to ensure compliance with this regulation and academic honesty standards.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft

claims.claim: The posted drafts of AR 5131.9 appear to draw no grade line, applying the same AI rule to every student.
claims.verbatim: Students are expected to use AI tools as an enhancement to their learning, not as a substitute for their intellectual work.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 draft
claims.notes: Absence claim. Full text extraction of documents 6187 and 6188 returned no grade level, grade band or age based rule. Say the AI rule is uniform, never that the district ruled out grade lines.

claims.claim: The VanBuskirk draft of AR 5131.9 permits AI as an instructional tool when it supports the objectives of the assignment.
claims.verbatim: Artificial intelligence (AI) may be used as an instructional tool when its use supports the educational objectives of the assignment and promotes student learning.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 VanBuskirk draft

claims.claim: The VanBuskirk draft of AR 5131.9 states that AI is meant to enhance learning and not to replace student thinking.
claims.verbatim: AI is intended to enhance learning, not replace the thinking, reasoning, creativity, and problem-solving through which students develop knowledge.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 5131.9 VanBuskirk draft

claims.claim: BP 6161.5 High-Quality Instruction and Purposeful Use of Technology came to the August 3rd committee as a brand new policy.
claims.verbatim: BP 6161.5 High-Quality Instruction and Purposeful Use of Technology is presented today in committee as a new policy at Administration's recommendation.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 was presented as the administrative regulation accompanying the newly drafted BP 6161.5.
claims.verbatim: AR 6161.5 High-Quality Instruction and Purposeful Use of Technology is presented in committee today as a new Administrative Regulation to accompany the newly drafted BP 6161.5 High-Quality Instruction and Purposeful Use of Technology at Administration's recommendation.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District
claims.notes: The minute caps live in AR 6161.5, the regulation, not in BP 6161.5, the policy.

claims.claim: BP 6161.5 states that technology is one instructional tool among many and is not the instructional program.
claims.verbatim: Technology is one of many instructional tools available to educators. It is not the instructional program.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, BP 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: BP 6161.5 says the board expects technology to support rather than replace relationships and instruction.
claims.verbatim: The Board expects technology to support, not replace, the relationships, instruction, and learning experiences that have the greatest impact on student success.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, BP 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 15 minutes a day in kindergarten and first grade.
claims.verbatim: Up to 15 minutes per instructional day
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 20 minutes a day in second grade.
claims.verbatim: Up to 20 minutes per instructional day
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 60 minutes a day in third grade.
claims.verbatim: Up to 60 minutes per instructional day
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 caps routine instructional technology use at 90 minutes a day in fourth and fifth grade.
claims.verbatim: Up to 90 minutes per instructional day
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 sets no routine daily technology limit for secondary schools.
claims.verbatim: routine daily technology limits are not established for secondary schools
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 addresses grades 6 through 12 with a qualitative standard instead of a minute figure.
claims.verbatim: Instructional technology in grades 6 through 12 will be purposeful, developmentally appropriate, and aligned with course objectives.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 says technology should not serve as the default instructional method where hands on learning offers greater educational value.
claims.verbatim: Not serve as the default instructional method when direct instruction, discussion, reading, writing, math, laboratory experiences, Career and Technical Education, fine arts, physical activity, or other hands-on learning opportunities provide greater educational value.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft
claims.notes: Districtwide expectation in a bulleted list, NOT a grades 6 through 12 clause. Never attribute it to older grades only.

claims.claim: AR 6161.5 excludes assessments, distance education and intervention services from the routine use it limits.
claims.verbatim: Routine instructional technical use does not include district or state assessments, short-term instructional projects, keyboarding instruction, computer skills instruction, digital research, Career and Technical Education activities, distance education, intervention services, or specialized instructional supports.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, AR 6161.5 draft

claims.claim: The screen time drafts BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5 do not mention artificial intelligence.
claims.verbatim: Technology is one of many instructional tools available to educators. It is not the instructional program.
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5 drafts
claims.notes: Absence claim verified by full text extraction of both snapshots. The minute caps are NOT an AI rule and the deck must never call them one.

claims.claim: The full board's regular business meeting on the evening of August 3rd took a first reading of BP 5131.9 Academic Honesty on its consent agenda.
claims.verbatim: REVISED (First Reading) BP 5131.9 Academic Honesty
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The August 3rd board consent agenda listed AR 5125 Student Records for first reading and action.
claims.verbatim: (First Reading & Action) AR 5125 Student Records
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The August 3rd board consent agenda listed BP 1114 Communication Using Electronic Media for first reading.
claims.verbatim: (First Reading) BP 1114 Communication Using Electronic Media
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The August 3rd board consent agenda also listed AR 6161.4 Acceptable Use Policy-Internet Safety Policy for first reading and action.
claims.verbatim: (First Reading & Action) AR 6161.4 Acceptable Use Policy-Internet Safety Policy
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The district describes the AR 5125 Student Records revisions as recommended by Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts.
claims.verbatim: AR 5125 Student Records was presented in committee on 07-06-2026 with minimal recommended revisions from Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The district describes the BP 1114 revisions as recommended by Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts.
claims.verbatim: BP 1114 - Communication Using Electronic Media was presented in committee on 07-06-2026 with minimal recommended revisions from Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The district describes the BP 5131.9 revisions as recommended by Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts.
claims.verbatim: BP 5131.9 Academic Honesty was presented in committee on 07-06-2026 with minimal recommended revisions from Administration regarding AI-related policy shifts.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The KPBSD board's regular business meeting on August 3rd began at 6:00 PM, eight hours after the policy committee convened.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The next regular KPBSD board meeting after August 3rd is scheduled for September 14, 2026.
claims.verbatim: September 14, 2026
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Board Meeting and Work Sessions Dates 2026-2027
claims.notes: Only the meeting date is verified. Tying any specific policy to it is an inference.

claims.claim: KPBSD reports an enrollment of about 8,300 students.
claims.verbatim: 8,301 students
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District
claims.notes: No stated as-of date. Never divide the 8,300 dollar MagicSchool figure by this; the near match is a coincidence.

claims.claim: KPBSD operates 39 schools.
claims.verbatim: 39 schools
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: KPBSD covers 25,600 square miles and employs 1,214 people.
claims.verbatim: 25,600 square miles
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: The first student day of the KPBSD 2026-27 school year is August 19, 2026 districtwide.
claims.verbatim: Student First August 19
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, 2026-2027 Districtwide Calendar
claims.notes: Six schools run variance calendars with their own start dates, so always write districtwide.

claims.claim: KPBSD teachers return on August 12, 2026, a week before students.
claims.verbatim: Teacher First August 12
claims.source_outlet: Kenai Peninsula Borough School District, 2026-2027 Districtwide Calendar
claims.notes: TENSE. The run date is 2026-08-09, so August 12th is still AHEAD. Never write that teachers came back. Inservice days are listed for August 12, 13, 14, 17 and 18.

claims.claim: Assistant superintendent Kari Dendurent said the district has spent 8,300 dollars to date on a three year MagicSchool subscription for students and staff.
claims.verbatim: Dendurent said the district has spent $8,300 to date on a three-year MagicSchool subscription for students and staff.
claims.source_outlet: KBBI AM 890
claims.notes: Single sourced official statement. Always attribute. No purchase record was reachable.

claims.claim: KBBI describes MagicSchool as an education specific AI platform that lets teachers and administrators monitor its use and set safeguards.
claims.verbatim: MagicSchool is an education-specific AI platform that allows teachers and school administrators to easily monitor the program's use and to implement safeguards.
claims.source_outlet: KBBI AM 890

claims.claim: MagicSchool markets itself on its homepage as safe district aligned AI for schools.
claims.verbatim: Save time, spark creativity, and support every student with safe, district-aligned AI.
claims.source_outlet: MagicSchool AI
claims.notes: Primary for what the company claims, not for what the product does.

claims.claim: Virtual learning coordinator Amanda Adams said the district group began last fall by comparing the state AI framework with what KPBSD already had.
claims.verbatim: One of the first things that that group did last fall was take a look at the framework, the AI framework that the state put out, and compare that with the training and decisions, and basic, basically overall philosophy and approach, and everything KPBSD had that was AI-related.
claims.source_outlet: KBBI AM 890

claims.claim: Alaska's state AI guidance for schools is titled Alaska's Strategic Framework, Artificial Intelligence for K-12, issued by the Department of Education and Early Development.
claims.verbatim: Alaska's Strategic Framework: Artificial Intelligence for K-12
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Education and Early Development
claims.notes: Marked v2.1 and carries no publication date. Never assert a publication date for it.

claims.claim: The Alaska DEED AI framework is built on seven guiding principles beginning with human-centered use.
claims.verbatim: AI must augment human capabilities, critical thinking, and creativity, never replacing human judgment or decision-making in educational contexts.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Education and Early Development
claims.notes: The seven are Human-Centered, Fair Access, Transparency, Oversight, Security, Ethical Use and Cultural Responsiveness.

claims.claim: The Alaska DEED AI framework's cultural responsiveness principle asks that AI tools affirm rather than diminish Alaska's diverse cultures.
claims.verbatim: AI tools should be critically evaluated and used to affirm, rather than diminish, the diverse cultures of Alaska.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Department of Education and Early Development

claims.claim: KDLL reported that the two technology policies presented on August 3rd need further committee review and full board approval before taking effect.
claims.verbatim: Both of the policies presented Monday are subject to additional review by the school board's Policy Committee. The policies require approval by the full board before going into effect.
claims.source_outlet: KDLL 91.9 FM

claims.claim: Superintendent Clayton Holland said board members have expressed a desire to put parameters on how much screen time students get in district buildings.
claims.verbatim: A lot of the school board members have expressed a desire to put some parameters on the amount of screen time that our students have in our buildings, and make sure that it's purposeful or intentional use of that time
claims.source_outlet: KDLL 91.9 FM

claims.claim: Board member Mica VanBuskirk said teachers should be able to say when AI use is acceptable and when it is not.
claims.verbatim: I think it's really important that we let teachers say, 'This is acceptable in this situation,' 'It's not acceptable in this situation.'
claims.source_outlet: KBBI AM 890

claims.claim: Assistant superintendent Kari Dendurent warned that strict parameters could limit the district as the language keeps changing.
claims.verbatim: If you are putting such strict parameters, it may really limit where we're going to be continuously changing the language.
claims.source_outlet: KBBI AM 890

claims.claim: KBBI reported in July that district administrators hope to implement the new AI policies by the beginning of the new school year.
claims.verbatim: District administrators hope to implement new AI policies by the beginning of the new school year.
claims.source_outlet: KBBI AM 890
claims.notes: A stated hope, never a commitment.

claims.claim: Kenai High School assistant principal Will Chervenak said the technology policy defines the district's ethos and its view of high quality instruction.
claims.verbatim: I really like the fact that this is a delineation that really defines our district and our ethos and the way that we think about high quality instruction and relationships and a focus on here in the district.
claims.source_outlet: KDLL 91.9 FM

claims.claim: The July 6th committee record shows the board asked for a demonstration or training on AI before settling the policies.
claims.verbatim: a demonstration or training for the Board on AI
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: KDLL reported that August 3rd was the first time board members saw the pair of screen time proposals.
claims.verbatim: School board members got their first look Monday at a pair of proposed policies that lay out screen time caps for certain grade levels, among other sideboards.
claims.source_outlet: KDLL 91.9 FM

claims.claim: No minutes are posted for either of the August 3rd meetings, so the outcome of that day is not on the public record.
claims.verbatim: This page could not be found.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District
claims.notes: Verified today by the showrunner. Both /meetings/666/minutes and /meetings/667/minutes render a 404 page. The July 6th minutes at /meetings/661/minutes render in full, so the 404 is an absence of posted minutes and not a broken route.

claims.claim: The July 6th committee minutes are posted and are marked approved on August 3, 2026, the same day whose own minutes are not posted.
claims.verbatim: Meeting Minutes-Approved (08-03-2026)
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District

claims.claim: Chair Kelley Cizek called the July 6th Policy Review Committee meeting to order at 1:03 p.m. with four board members and the assistant superintendent present.
claims.verbatim: Chair Cizek called the meeting to order at 1:03 p.m.
claims.source_outlet: KPBSD E-Governance, Kenai Peninsula Borough School District
claims.notes: Members present were Kelley Cizek, Board President Jason Tauriainen, Mica Vanbuskirk, Ash-Lee Waddell (virtual) and Assistant Superintendent Kari Dendurent.

killed.claim: The August 3rd Policy Review Committee agenda had eight items
killed.why: The fetched agenda has six numbered top level sections. Eight is the count of policy and exhibit documents inside them, preserved as C03.

killed.claim: A first board policy committee discussion of the three proposed AI policies happened on July 7th, 2026
killed.why: Every KPBSD item page dates the committee presentation to 07-06-2026. July 7th is wrong.

killed.claim: Alaska DEED published its AI guidance in October 2025
killed.why: The DEED page and the framework PDF both carry no publication date. The framework survives as C45 without a date.

killed.claim: AR 5131.9 was rewritten by a district AI committee
killed.why: The district's own item description credits Administration. No fetched page connects the AI review group to authorship.

killed.claim: The screen time caps are part of the district's AI policy
killed.why: Full text extraction of BP 6161.5 and AR 6161.5 returned no occurrence of AI or artificial intelligence. Conflating them would be this deck's most likely factual error. See C26.

killed.claim: The draft says technology should not be the default instruction method in grades 6 through 12
killed.why: That sentence is a districtwide bulleted expectation, not a secondary clause. Survives as C24 with the grade attribution removed.

killed.claim: The Policy Review Committee advanced, postponed or amended its August 3rd items
killed.why: No minutes are posted. Now carried as claim C56, an absence verified today against both August 3rd minutes pages. The OUTCOME still must not be asserted; only the absence of a posted outcome may be stated.

killed.claim: The full board approved the AI policies on August 3rd
killed.why: No minutes for meeting 667 were reachable. Write what the agenda scheduled, never what the board did.

killed.claim: MagicSchool is used by a stated number of educators or districts
killed.why: No user, educator or district counts are published on the vendor homepage.

killed.claim: Will Chervenak is assistant principal at Kenai Central High School
killed.why: KDLL says Kenai High School. Quote survives as C53 with KDLL's wording.

killed.claim: The board will take up the screen time policies at a specific named meeting
killed.why: No source names it. September 14, 2026 is verified as a meeting date only, in C35.

killed.claim: The 8,300 dollar MagicSchool figure is a district purchase record
killed.why: Killed as a primary figure only. Survives as C41, an official's statement to a newsroom. Never present it as audited and never divide it by enrollment.
